When sample $S(x+1, y+1, z+1)$ arrives, the unit completes the gradient estimation for $S(x, y, z)$ [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the Gradient Estimation unit operates 'one voxel, one beam, and one slice behind the Interpolation unit.' It further explains that this delay is necessary to ensure sufficient data is available (previous, current, and next slices) for gradient calculation. Since the Interpolation unit processes sample $S(x, y, z)$ at a given time, the Gradient Estimation unit, being delayed by one unit in the pipeline, will process the gradient for that specific sample $S(x, y, z)$ when the next sample $S(x+1, y+1, z+1)$ arrives (or effectively, the gradient estimation for a sample occurs one cycle/step after its interpolation). The claim accurately reflects the pipeline latency and relative positioning described in the source.
